mechanism_narrative: Grocery and pharmacy mobility remains stable (GROCERY_PHARM at -17.0%, flat across four weeks) while retail collapses (-63.0%), indicating essential-goods shopping is decoupled from discretionary retail. This stability signals that essential-trip infrastructure persists, but retail suppression reflects policy-driven closures, not transport failure. Retail will remain depressed for four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM variance < 3 percentage points AND RETAIL_REC variance > 20 percentage points
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM volatility exceeds 3 percentage points week-on-week, indicating supply-chain disruption that would force retail reopening.

failure_condition: PARKS recovers above -3% within one week, or RETAIL_REC rises above -55% in the immediate week following.

failure_condition: WORKPLACES recovers above -35% or RESIDENTIAL falls below 12% within two weeks, or RETAIL_REC rises above -50%.

This is an always-on mechanism in high-transit-dependent cities.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -59.6%, worst of all categories
failure_condition: TRANSIT recovers above -40% within four weeks, or RETAIL_REC rises above -40% despite continued transit suppression.
